title: You're Copying the People You Like — Right Now, Without Knowing It
description:
You are unconsciously copying the postures and mannerisms of the people you like — and the people you mimic feel more connected to you as a result. Chartrand and Bargh's 1999 chameleon effect research revealed that automatic mimicry is one of the core mechanisms of human rapport. This video breaks down the research, why the brain does it, and how to use this knowledge to connect more genuinely.

**What you'll learn:**
• What the chameleon effect is and how Chartrand and Bargh studied it
• Why being mimicked produces stronger liking and smoother interaction
• Why the brain mimics — the social bonding function
• How to use this ethically and genuinely
